notes: muse is a single-birth FilesUnderRoot adapter (no presession proc-<PID> split needed — 1-1_session-start and 2-1_basic-turn both anchor session_birth directly at 'start'), so unlike claudecode's spec this does not model a presession row. session_birth/pid_bind cover the FIRST session (V1); v1_turn_start/v1_turn_end cover its no-op turn; v2_session_birth (new_session:true) is the /clear-minted second session (V2), a genuinely different UUIDv7 per the live probe; old_session_ended asserts transcript_removed pinned to V1 specifically (same_session_as:session_birth) — this is the load-bearing same-PID-cleanup signal (pid_manager.go cleanupStalePIDHolders, the same generic #169 mechanism claudecode's own session-reset cell relies on) and is what would go red if the daemon ever just let V1 linger; v2_turn_start/v2_turn_end are pinned to v2_session_birth so a stale match against V1's turn arc can't vacuously satisfy them. old_session_ended's max_delay_ms is generous (5000ms) to cover DiscoverPIDWithRetry's 0/500ms/1s/2s retry schedule for V2's own PID discovery, which is the trigger for the cleanup. Driver gap: reset_session is not yet implemented in driver-interactive.sh (record ports it). Not yet live-recorded against an attached daemon — daemon=full is provisional per the metadata's caveats.
source: of scenario show --name session-reset; live probe (this assessment) of muse /clear in a throwaway tmux dir

text: First muse session (V1) appears in ready shortly after the TUI finishes launching
muse-bin PID bound to V1 via its .session.lock held flock fd
First no-op prompt (run started) drives V1 ready → working
First turn completes (run terminal:completed) back to ready on V1; no tool call
Spec: 'new session appears in ready with a NEW session_id' — /clear mints a genuinely new UUIDv7 session directory (V2), born directly in ready like any muse session

Spec: 'old session disappears' — pid_manager.go's cleanupStalePIDHolders reaps V1 once V2's own PID discovery resolves to the SAME pid V1 was already bound to (the generic #169 same-PID cleanup path); bounded to cover DiscoverPIDWithRetry's retry schedule
Second prompt drives the NEW session (V2) ready → working — must NOT match a stale transition on V1
Second turn completes back to ready on V2; no tool call
